payload.title: Whether a vite config declares federation exposes is read twice, by an AST property-name test in bundle-budget-adapter.ts and by the regex _MF_EXPOSES_RE in aria_kernel/recursive_impact.py, and the two disagree on exposes: {}, on a non-literal value and on which config file names count, with nothing pinning them together.
evidence: tools/aria-adapters/bundle-budget-adapter.ts:109-117 (any property named exposes at any depth makes the config a remote)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/recursive_impact.py:743-746 (the regex needs exposes, a colon and a brace block)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/recursive_impact.py:764-775 (the kernel considers vite.config.ts and module-federation.config files only)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/recursive_impact.py:801-812 (the kernel records an exposes entry only when keys are found)
payload.rule_violated: Single owner of one fact (CLAUDE.md Architectural Approach tier 2 or 3): what makes a vite config a federated remote is decided once or pinned.
payload.notes: With exposes: {} or exposes: exposesMap in web/modules/x/vite.config.ts the adapter treats the module as a federated remote and runs the route-page rule on it, while the kernel's impact graph records no exposed keys for the same file; a vite.config.mts remote is visible to the adapter and invisible to the kernel. The agreement on the 8 real remotes is not pinned, so a change to the federation plugin option moves only one reader. Close condition: Compute the remote set once (one reader whose result the other consumes) or add an invariant that evaluates both readers over every web/modules/*/vite.config.* and asserts the same remote set, with fixtures for an empty exposes object and a non-literal value. Plan row: DET detector program (landing batch 3). Verified at origin/main d716541239.
